ai.description: This 45–55 mm frog is olive-green with distinct dark transverse lines across the back. It features large, fully webbed feet and prominent white spots on the flanks.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Medog Flying Frog is best distinguished by the distinct, thin, dark transverse lines across its dorsal surface, which are absent in other similar Indian rhacophorids.
ai.habitat: The Medog Flying Frog inhabits subtropical evergreen broadleaf forests in the Eastern Himalayas, typically at elevations ranging from 1,400 to 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Medog flying frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining inactive in tree hollows or under leaves during the day and emerging at night to hunt for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Rhacophorus translineatus* breeds during the monsoon season, depositing foam nests on vegetation overhanging water. Specific clutch size data remains undocumented.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Rhacophorus translineatus* occurs in the Eastern Himalayas of Arunachal Pradesh, India, typically inhabiting high-elevation forests between 1,500 and 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Medog Flying Frog produces a series of high-pitched, rhythmic "peep" notes, typically heard emanating from dense vegetation near streams in its humid forest habitat.
